title: Consumer parenting app (iOS app + marketing/editorial site) web-generation policy

classification.marketModel: direct-to-consumer mobile app (App Store) with a free tier and a family subscription

consumerAppSignals.claim: every primary CTA is an App Store download via an attribution OneLink
footer ships an official 'Download on the App Store' badge
pricing is a consumer family subscription (one paid plan from $9.99/month, one free plan), not B2B tiers or seats
the paid plan is framed for households ('families who parent as a team', caregiver logins), not organisations
consumerAppSignals.anchor: description: 'For families who parent as a team'

consumerAppSignals.claim: audience is parents (reviews by mums and dads of babies)
consumerAppSignals.anchor: name: 'Max L., Dad of Baby R (1 mo)'

consumerAppSignals.claim: the editorial blog covers sleep, feeding, development, health, pregnancy

classificationEvidence.saasSignalsAbsent: grep of src/components and src/pages (2026-10-29): no 'enterprise', no book/request-a-demo, no dashboard, no integrations, no per-seat/per-user pricing, no sign-in route. The comparison table compares the app with consumer alternatives (search, forums, chatbots, books), not B2B tools.

notBoundTo.n0-saas-design-constraints-common: Explicitly NOT applied. That policy assumes a B2B SaaS product (pricing tiers for teams, dashboards, feature matrices against vendors, integrations, demo funnels). Riley is a direct-to-consumer parenting app distributed through the App Store; its site is marketing + editorial content for parents. Binding to the SaaS policy would require a recorded architecture decision, which has not been made.

generationRules: Pages are drawn only from the 8 templates (7 families) and 36 section contracts in this repo; no new section types.

No B2B constructs: no seat/tier pricing tables, vendor feature matrices, integrations grids, dashboards, demo-request or changelog sections. The only pricing construct is pricing-hero (max 2 consumer plans) and the only comparison construct is the gradient-band comparison table, both because the clone really has them; their prices, plan names and competitor names are operator-supplied in generation mode (GENERATION_MODE_CLAIM / GENERATION_MODE_CUSTOMER).

App-store download CTAs: in generation mode store badges are operator-supplied official artwork (role user-supplied-asset) and links are placeholder-url (.example/.invalid) until the operator wires its own store listing; Riley's OneLink, App Store marks and 'Download on the' wording are rejected (GENERATION_MODE_STORE).

Child and parent imagery is must-not-fabricate: no real photos (lifestyle, user stories, article covers, author/clinician portraits) in generation mode; use generated illustrations or fictional avatars, never photorealistic children presented as real (GENERATION_MODE_PERSON / GENERATION_MODE_ASSET).

Health and development claims are must-not-fabricate: no clinical/medical endorsements, efficacy claims, SIDS/safety claims, statistics or invented citations in generation mode (GENERATION_MODE_CLAIM, policy list in schema/leakage-patterns.json). Article sources are operator-supplied or left empty.

Proof is never invented: clinician names/credentials, testimonials and ratings must be operator-verified; generation examples use bracketed placeholders, and rating/review-count wording is rejected (GENERATION_MODE_RATING).
Legal pages: no policy text is generated; the policy-embed slot points at an operator-supplied URL (GENERATION_MODE_EMBED).
Riley brand, mascots, illustrations, Rive chat screens, copy (5-word shingles), people and URLs never appear in generation mode (GENERATION_MODE_BRAND / _ASSET / _SCREENSHOT / _COPY / _URL).

approval.note: Classification and rules are defined here by an agent (agent attestation, not a human sign-off). A human architecture owner must ratify the non-SaaS binding before it replaces any shared common policy; licensing of real assets and medical-content review remain open.
